rules.name: Approved company IR page registry lifecycle
rules.plainEnglish: A ticker's IR page entry moves through these states. Missing gives NOT_REGISTERED; candidate gives CANDIDATE_AVAILABLE (not fetched, decisionGrade false); disabled gives DISABLED; approved but past revalidateAfter gives REVALIDATION_DUE (skipped); fetch or allow-list failure gives SOURCE_VALIDATION_FAILED; a successful fetch gives APPROVED_SOURCE_OK, or EMPTY_RESULT if nothing falls in the window.
rules.given: registry entry IQE.L with status 'candidate' (registryVersion 2026-09-25.1200)
rules.then: no fetch happens; warning COMPANY_IR_PAGE_CANDIDATE_AVAILABLE; status CANDIDATE_AVAILABLE; allowedAction review_and_promote; coverage PARTIAL
rules.parameters: allowedAction: APPROVED_SOURCE_OK->fetch_configured_source, CANDIDATE_AVAILABLE->review_and_promote, else registry_review_required; fetch only https and allowedHosts+allowedPathPrefixes; max body 750 KB; timeout 15s; HTML parsing capped at 50 blocks; titles under 6 chars dropped
rules.smeQuestion: Any status other than 'disabled' or 'candidate' (e.g. 'rejected', blank, or a typo) is treated as approved, fetched, and its items stamped approvalStatus='approved'. An unparseable revalidateAfter counts as not fresh, which gives REVALIDATION_DUE

rules.given: Registry entry for XYZ with status 'candidate'
rules.then: Nothing is fetched. Warning COMPANY_IR_PAGE_CANDIDATE_AVAILABLE with candidate decisionGrade=false, sourceStatus CANDIDATE_AVAILABLE, allowedAction review_and_promote

edgeCases: A missing revalidateAfter counts as fresh, while an unparseable revalidateAfter counts as stale

rules.name: Legacy company_ir source: Python serves it from Yahoo news, Worker from official RSS discovery
rules.source: server.py:2517-2522; server.py:2608-2627; server.py:2243; server.py:2399-2405; worker/src/yahoo-finance.ts:11769-11775; worker/src/yahoo-finance.ts:11785-11789; worker/src/yahoo-finance.ts:10972-10994
rules.plainEnglish: When a caller selects 'company_ir', the Python server fetches the Yahoo news tab and returns Yahoo items under it, while the Worker runs company-website RSS/Atom discovery. The resulting items, evidence class and status are different.
rules.given: sources=['company_ir'] for AAPL
rules.then: Yahoo news/press items (sourceType yahoo_finance_news) are returned and 'company_ir' is marked used. The status counts only sourceType company_ir/press_release items, so sourceStatus.company_ir = EMPTY_RESULT even though items were returned, or PROVIDER_ERROR if any Yahoo warning exists. rules.parameters: Python company_ir item types: company_ir, press_release
edgeCases: Python never emits WEBSITE_NOT_AVAILABLE / DISCOVERY_* / FEED_NOT_FOUND / PARSE_ERROR, although its coverage code recognises them
Contextual Yahoo news is presented under a source name that implies official IR evidence

rules.name: Evidence class, ticker match and decision use labeling
rules.plainEnglish: Every returned item gets an evidence class and a decisionUse. Only resolved SEC EX-99 exhibits and approved IR-page items are USE_OFFICIAL_EVIDENCE. Other official or wire sources are CHECK_OFFICIAL_RELEASES. Yahoo and Finnhub news is CHECK_OFFICIAL_RELEASES only for material event types, otherwise CONTEXT_ONLY.
rules.given: A Finnhub item (sourceType company_news) with eventType 'analyst'
rules.then: evidenceClass CONTEXTUAL_NEWS, decisionUse CONTEXT_ONLY, urlProvenance PUBLISHER (or PROVIDER if the host is finance.yahoo.com/finnhub.io)
rules.parameters: Material Yahoo event types: earnings, guidance, contract, financing, product, regulatory, litigation
edgeCases: tickerMatch is EXPLICIT if matchBasis is one of the explicit types or the ticker word appears; SOURCE_SCOPED if a tickers list exists; else UNVERIFIED. Since every item carries tickers=[ticker], UNVERIFIED is effectively unreachable

rules.name: Press release decision-grade and status precedence
rules.plainEnglish: A press release result is decision-grade only when an 8-K's EX-99.1 exhibit is resolved or an approved IR-page item with a URL is found. Status precedence is SEC_EX99_FOUND, then APPROVED_IR_PAGE_FOUND, then SEC_8K_FOUND_EX99_NOT_FOUND, then a source-specific not-found status.
rules.given: Defaults (sec, company_ir_page, yahoo_finance_press_releases). One 8-K is found whose EX-99.1 does not resolve, and there is no approved IR page
rules.then: status=SEC_8K_FOUND_EX99_NOT_FOUND, coverageStatus same, decisionGrade=false, failureMode=SEC_8K_FOUND_EX99_NOT_FOUND, and warning SEC_8K_FOUND_EX99_NOT_FOUND with filingsSearched=1
rules.parameters: SEC types limited to 8-K; EX-99.1 resolution concurrency 4; secEvidence and irPageEvidence capped at 10; default lookback 90, max 20
edgeCases: With no release items: NO_YAHOO_PRESS_RELEASE if Yahoo PR was selected, else COMPANY_IR_PAGE_NOT_APPROVED, else COMPANY_IR_NOT_FOUND, else NOT_FOUND
A resolved EX-99.1 rewrites the item to sourceType sec_ex99_found with confidence HIGH

rules.name: Verify NOT_FOUND upgraded to SOURCE_LIMITED_NOT_FOUND
rules.plainEnglish: If nothing was found but coverage was incomplete, the result becomes SOURCE_LIMITED_NOT_FOUND with a failure mode chosen in priority order. It is retryable only for subrequest limits, rate limits and timeouts.
rules.given: No matches. Finnhub status RATE_LIMITED
rules.then: status=SOURCE_LIMITED_NOT_FOUND, failureMode=RATE_LIMITED, retryable=true, plus a recommendedAction to retry without the failed providers
rules.parameters: Failure-mode order: WORKER_SUBREQUEST_LIMIT (warning text 'too many subrequests'), RATE_LIMITED, PROVIDER_TIMEOUT, PROVIDER_CHANGED, YAHOO_IDENTITY_UNAVAILABLE, SOURCE_UNCONFIGURED, SOURCE_NOT_ELIGIBLE, PROVIDER_ERROR
edgeCases: IR-page registry states (NOT_REGISTERED, etc.) do not trigger the upgrade here even though they make coverage PARTIAL
rules.smeQuestion:
P0 panel doubts spec fidelity: P0 is justified on data integrity and compliance grounds. The rule stops a search with incomplete provider coverage (rate limit, timeout, subrequest cap) from being reported as confirmed absence (NOT_FOUND) of an SEC filing, earnings or corporate event. A silent regression would turn 'the search failed' into 'the event didn't happen', which auditors and controllers would care about. It also sets the failureMode and retryable output contract fields. However, the citation is wrong. server.py:2411-2439 is the company_ir_page/newswire source-status mapping and server.py:3384-3394 is ticker/company-name relevance scoring. Neither contains the NOT_FOUND upgrade, the failure-mode order or the retryable check. The rule text matches the real code, which is at server.py:2458-2486 (_verify_coverage_failure_mode). The order there matches the card exactly: 'too many subrequests' in SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE warnings, then RATE_LIMITED, TIMEOUT->PROVIDER_TIMEOUT, PROVIDER_CHANGED, IDENTITY_UNAVAILABLE->YAHOO_IDENTITY_UNAVAILABLE, UNCONFIGURED, NOT_ELIGIBLE, PROVIDER_ERROR. The rest is at server.py:3436-3473: the upgrade at 3437, retryable limited to WORKER_SUBREQUEST_LIMIT/RATE_LIMITED/PROVIDER_TIMEOUT at 3446, and the recommendedAction to retry without the failed providers at 3470-3473. Finnhub RATE_LIMITED is set at server.py:1961 (HTTP 402/429) and 2361, so the example scenario holds. The citation must be corrected to 2458-2486 and 3436-3473 before this becomes a contract. Gaps for the planner: AUTH_ERROR and the company_ir_page/discovery statuses (CANDIDATE_AVAILABLE, NOT_REGISTERED, DISABLED, FEED_NOT_FOUND, etc.) make coverage PARTIAL (server.py:2449) but have no failure mode, so NOT_FOUND is not upgraded when only those fail. That looks like a real data-integrity gap, and deciding it is reserved for the planner. No instruction-like text or credentials in the lines read. | The citation is wrong. server.py:2411-2439 is the company_ir_page and newswire per-source status mapping inside _compute_source_status. server.py:3384-3394 is the ticker and company-name matching inside _relevance_score. Neither range contains the NOT_FOUND to SOURCE_LIMITED_NOT_FOUND upgrade, the failure-mode order, or the retryable logic. Judged only against the cited code, the rule is not supported.

The behaviour itself does exist elsewhere in the same file, and it matches the rule:
- server.py:2458-2486 (_verify_coverage_failure_mode) checks in this order: WORKER_SUBREQUEST_LIMIT, RATE_LIMITED, TIMEOUT (reported as PROVIDER_TIMEOUT), PROVIDER_CHANGED, IDENTITY_UNAVAILABLE (reported as YAHOO_IDENTITY_UNAVAILABLE), UNCONFIGURED (reported as SOURCE_UNCONFIGURED), NOT_ELIGIBLE (reported as SOURCE_NOT_ELIGIBLE), PROVIDER_ERROR. Otherwise it returns None.
- server.py:3436-3473 upgrades NOT_FOUND to SOURCE_LIMITED_NOT_FOUND only when a failure mode exists. It also adds a warning that carries the failureMode, sets retryable to true only for WORKER_SUBREQUEST_LIMIT, RATE_LIMITED or PROVIDER_TIMEOUT, and sets the recommendedAction text to "retry with a narrower sources list that excludes failed providers". So the example (no matches, Finnhub rate-limited, giving SOURCE_LIMITED_NOT_FOUND, RATE_LIMITED, retryable=true, plus a recommendedAction) is right.

Details the card misses or states too broadly:
1. "too many subrequests" is only looked for in the messages of warnings whose code is SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE. It is matched case-insensitively against all those messages joined together.
2. "Coverage was incomplete" is too broad. Several statuses make _compute_source_coverage return PARTIAL (server.py:2448-2453) but produce no failure mode: AUTH_ERROR, WEBSITE_NOT_AVAILABLE, DISCOVERY_NOT_FOUND, DISCOVERY_BUDGET_EXHAUSTED, FEED_NOT_FOUND, PARSE_ERROR, and the company_ir_page states CANDIDATE_AVAILABLE, NOT_REGISTERED, DISABLED, REVALIDATION_DUE and SOURCE_VALIDATION_FAILED. In those cases the result stays NOT_FOUND even though coverage was incomplete. This is an edge case equivalence testing must cover, and the planner may need to decide whether it is intended.
3. The upgrade only applies when the status is NOT_FOUND. CONFIRMED, PARTIAL, STALE and CONFLICTING are never upgraded. failureMode, retryable=true and recommendedAction are only set on SOURCE_LIMITED_NOT_FOUND results; every other result gets failureMode=None, retryable=false and recommendedAction=None.
4. A separate, similar rule exists in _build_collection_status (server.py:2172-2189). It produces SOURCE_LIMITED_NOT_FOUND from warning codes, including any COMPANY_IR_PAGE_* code, and should not be mixed up with this one.

The P0 rating is reasonable on data-integrity grounds. The rule stops a "we could not reach the sources" result from being reported as "this event did not happen", and the retryable flag tells clients whether to retry. The citation should be changed to server.py:2458-2486 and 3436-3473 before this becomes a contract. The cited lines contain no injection-style text and no credentials.

rules.given: sources=['company_ir'] for ticker AAPL
rules.then: Worker: items come only from company-domain or identity-matched feeds, and status follows the RSS discovery outcome. Python: Yahoo feed items are returned, sourcesUsed includes company_ir, and company_ir status is OK/EMPTY_RESULT based on items with sourceType company_ir/press_release.
rules.parameters: none
edgeCases: The Python get_company_news docstring says company_ir is 'RSS/Atom only', which contradicts the Python code
rules.smeQuestion: Should Python implement the Worker's RSS/Atom autodiscovery for company_ir, or should company_ir in Python stop reporting itself as used when it only relays Yahoo items?

rules.name: Company IR page URL allow-list
rules.plainEnglish: IR page fetches and item links must be https, on a host in the entry's allowedHosts (ignoring a leading www.), and under one of its allowedPathPrefixes. Off-list redirects or items are refused, and responses over 750 KiB are refused.
rules.given: Entry allowedHosts ['investor.acme.com'], prefixes ['/news']. An item links to http://investor.acme.com/news/x
rules.then: The item is dropped (scheme is not https). A redirect to https://evil.com fails the whole source with COMPANY_IR_PAGE_VALIDATION_FAILED
rules.parameters: Max size 750*1024 bytes; timeout 15s; HTML parsing limited to the first 50 blocks; titles under 6 characters skipped

rules.name: EX-99.1 press-release exhibit identification and filer CIK selection
rules.plainEnglish: An 8-K is upgraded to a decision-grade press release (sec_ex99_found) only when an EX-99.1 exhibit is found. The two runtimes find the exhibit and the CIK in different ways.
rules.given: An 8-K whose index lists an exhibit typed 'EX-99' described as 'Press Release', and an item URL without /data/<cik>/ but with cikInt=320193
rules.then: Worker: CIK comes from item cikInt, then the URL, then the accession prefix. The exhibit matches if its type starts with EX-99.1/EX-99.01, or its type starts with EX-99 and the description says PRESS/EARNINGS/RESULTS RELEASE, or the filename matches ex99_1, with an HTML index scan as fallback. Result: SEC_EX99_FOUND and decisionGrade=true. Python: CIK comes only from the URL /data/<cik>/ and the exhibit type must be exactly EX-99.1, EX-99 or 99.1. Result: SEC_8K_FOUND_EX99_NOT_FOUND and decisionGrade=false.
rules.parameters: Python EX-99.1 concurrency 4; Worker HTML index read cap 100,000 bytes
edgeCases: Python accepts a bare 'EX-99' type of any description; the Worker requires release wording for plain EX-99
The Worker uses the accession prefix CIK last because it identifies the filer agent
rules.suspectedDefect: Python/TS divergence on the decision-grade gate: the same filing can produce decisionGrade true in one runtime and false in the other.

rules.name: Analyst price target extraction from news sentences (four patterns, fixed precedence)
rules.plainEnglish: A price target is read from a news sentence by trying four phrasings in order: 'target from X to Y', 'target to Y from X', '$Y price target', then 'price target ... Y'. A number followed by '%' is never treated as a target.
rules.given: A sentence 'Needham raises its price target from $80 to $95' (or 'PT to 120p from 100p', or 'Cantor reiterates $122 target', or 'price target implies 25% upside')
rules.when: The extractor looks for a price target
rules.then: Results: target 95, prior 80, currency USD; target 120, prior 100, currency GBp; target 122, prior null, USD; the '25% upside' sentence gives no target. Thousands separators are removed ('1,250' becomes 1250).
rules.and: from/to and to/from are tried first; '$N target' is tried before the generic 'target ... N' scan. A trigger phrase is 'price target', 'target price', 'PT' or 'price objective'. Up to 40 non-period characters may sit between the trigger and the number.
rules.parameters: Trigger-to-number gap: 40 chars; precedence FROM_TO > TO_FROM > BEFORE > TO; percent lookahead (?![\d.,]*\s?%)
edgeCases: The percent guard rejects '25%' even when backtracking to the '2'
TARGET_BEFORE accepts only $, US$, GBP sign, EUR sign and NT$ symbols; 'SEK 92 target' falls through to the generic pattern
The regexes ignore case, but currency mapping does not: 'usd 95' captures a currency token that maps to null

rules.name: Analyst price target parsing precedence and currency
rules.plainEnglish: A price target is read from a sentence in fixed order: 'target from X to Y', then 'target to Y from X', then '$N price target', then 'target ... N'; a number followed by % is never a target, and the currency is inferred from the symbol or a pence/kr suffix.
rules.given: Sentence 'Cantor raises price target from $100 to $122'
rules.then: priceTarget = {target:122, prior:100, currency:'USD'}
rules.and: 'Peel Hunt price target 450p' yields {target:450, prior:null, currency:'GBp'}; 'price target cut 12%' yields no target.
rules.parameters: Trigger phrases: price target, target price, PT, price objective; max 40-char gap between phrase and number; currency map $/US$/USD->USD, GBP/£->GBP, GBp/GBX/p/pence->GBp, €/EUR->EUR, SEK/kr->SEK, NT$/TWD->TWD; anything else -> null
edgeCases: Thousands separators are stripped before parsing
TARGET_BEFORE only recognises $, US$, £, €, NT$ symbols (not codes like USD)
An unrecognised currency symbol yields currency null rather than an error

rules.name: Brokerage firm attribution for a news item
rules.plainEnglish: Each news item is credited to the analyst firm named earliest in its text. Firms from recent rating changes are searched first, then a fixed list of about 70 brokers. Matching is case-sensitive.
rules.given: Rating changes name 'Cantor Fitzgerald', and an item reads 'Morgan Stanley and Cantor Fitzgerald lift targets'
rules.then: firm = 'Morgan Stanley' (earliest match position). On a tie at the same position, the longer name wins ('Bernstein SocGen' over 'Bernstein').
rules.and: A firm match must not be preceded or followed by a letter. A broker already in the rating-change list (case-insensitive) is not added again. One firm is assigned per item, not per sentence.
rules.parameters: Built-in broker list of about 70 names (Morgan Stanley ... Arctic)
edgeCases: 'benchmark' in lower case does not match the firm Benchmark
One firm per item: an item quoting two brokers credits every sentence to the first-named one

rules.name: Company IR page record extraction (JSON vs HTML)
rules.plainEnglish: Approved IR pages are parsed as JSON when the adapter is 'structured' or the content type contains json, and as HTML otherwise. In HTML, article blocks are used; if there are none, list items mentioning release keywords are used. Only the first 50 blocks are read, and titles shorter than 6 characters are dropped.
rules.given: An HTML IR page with no <article> tags and 80 <li> items, 60 of which mention 'announces'
rules.then: Only the first 50 qualifying <li> blocks are examined. Each title comes from the first h1-h4 heading, or failing that the first anchor's text. Its date comes from <time datetime> or the time element's text. Items are then filtered by the date window and truncated to max_results
rules.parameters: Block cap 50; minimum title length 6; li keywords: press release, news release, earnings, results, announces, reports. JSON list keys tried in order: items, releases, pressReleases, news, data, feed.items, data.* values. JSON title keys: title/headline/name. JSON date keys: publishedAt/published_at/datePublished/date_published/date/pubDate
edgeCases: JSON records without a title are skipped
Items whose resolved URL fails the allow-list are dropped
Items without a publish date always fail the date window and are excluded

rules.name: Duplicate group id hashing
rules.plainEnglish: A duplicate group id is the first 16 hex characters of SHA-256 of 'normalized title stem|publish day|upper-cased issuer or ticker'. No id is produced when both the title stem and the day are empty.
rules.given: ticker 'ACME', title 'ACME Corp Announces Q3 Results', publishedAt '2026-10-01T13:00:00Z', issuer 'Acme Corp'
rules.when: The duplicate group id is computed
rules.then: key = 'announces q3 results|2026-10-01|ACME CORP' and id = sha256(key)[:16]
rules.parameters: Hash length 16 hex characters; the day is the first 10 characters of publishedAt
edgeCases: The url argument is accepted but not used in the key
The same story from different issuers' feeds hashes differently if the issuer strings differ

rules.name: Duplicate group key
rules.plainEnglish: Items are treated as the same event when they share the normalized headline (first 80 characters, with the ticker, URLs and boilerplate words removed), the publish date, and the issuer (or the ticker if there is no issuer).
rules.given: 'NVIDIA Corp Announces Q3 Results - GlobeNewswire' and 'Nvidia announces Q3 results', both on 2026-10-10, no issuer
rules.then: Both produce stem 'nvidia announces q3 results' (corp/globenewswire removed), day 2026-10-10, entity NVDA, so the sha256 prefixes are identical (16 hex characters)
rules.parameters: _DEDUP_TITLE_MAX_LEN=80; stop terms yahoo, finance, finnhub, globenewswire, press, release, inc, corp, corporation, company, plc, ltd, llc
edgeCases: If both the title stem and the date are empty, there is no key, a DEDUPE_WEAK_KEY warning is raised, and the item passes through undeduped
An issuer set on one copy but not the other gives different keys

rules.name: Duplicate news collapse by source priority
rules.plainEnglish: Items sharing a normalised-title + day + entity key are merged. The higher-priority source is kept (SEC 0 > IR 1 > press release 2 > newswire 3 > Finnhub 4 > Yahoo news 5 > Marketaux 6 > other 7), with the newer timestamp breaking ties. The losers are kept as sourceRefs, and a non-blocking TIMESTAMP_VARIANCE warning is raised when timestamps differ.
rules.given: the same headline on 2026-10-01 from Finnhub (rank 4) and Yahoo news (rank 5)
rules.then: the Finnhub item is kept with the Yahoo item in sourceRefs. Results are sorted newest first
rules.parameters: title stem max 80 chars; key hash sha256 truncated to 16 hex characters; stop terms yahoo, finance, finnhub, globenewswire, press, release, inc, corp ...
edgeCases: Items without a duplicateGroupId pass through un-deduped

rules.and: Metric normalisation: EV/EBITDA->EBITDA (EV), EV/EBIT->EBIT (EV), EV/sales or EV/revenue->sales (EV), P/E, price-to-earnings, earnings or EPS->earnings, price-to-sales, revenue or sales->sales, FCF or free cash flow->free cash flow, plus gross profit, book value and NAV. enterpriseValue is also true when 'EV' or 'enterprise value' appears in the window. Duplicates (same multiple, metric and EV flag) are kept once. The multiple must be greater than 0.
rules.parameters: Multiple digits 1-3 (max 999.x); multiple-first gap 40 chars; metric-first trailing window 30 chars; exclusion words than|grew|growth|increase(s|d)|faster|more; period tokens FY/CY/F+yy(yy)[E], 1H/2H+yy[E], 19xx/20xx[E], NTM, 'next twelve months' (becomes NTM), 'forward'
edgeCases: The metric-first form allows hedges 'about', 'roughly', 'approximately' and '~'
Periods are de-duplicated and upper-cased with whitespace removed ('FY 26E' becomes 'FY26E')
A bare four-digit year in the window counts as a period

rules.name: Verify event query term threshold
rules.plainEnglish: Generic words (announce, results, report, update, etc.) and words under 3 letters are dropped. An item matches if the whole normalized query appears as a phrase, or if it contains (stemmed) all of the meaningful terms when there are 2 or fewer, or ceil(67%) of them when there are more.
rules.given: event_query 'BlueBird satellite launch contract announced'
rules.then: meaningfulTerms=[bluebird, satellite, launch, contract], and requiredTermMatches=ceil(4*0.67)=3
rules.parameters: Ratio 0.67; min term length 3; stopword list at server.py:3196-3201
edgeCases: A query with no meaningful terms adds EVENT_QUERY_TOO_GENERIC
rules.suspectedDefect: An exact PHRASE match is accepted even when the query is entirely generic (e.g. 'announced results'), so a too-generic query can still produce matches and a CONFIRMED status despite the EVENT_QUERY_TOO_GENERIC warning.
rules.smeQuestion: Should a PHRASE match be allowed when meaningfulTerms is empty?

rules.name: Yahoo company identity aliases and acronyms
rules.plainEnglish: The company's short and long names are normalised and stripped of legal suffixes to form match aliases (min 3 chars), and their initials (ignoring the/and/of/for) form acronyms of 3-6 letters; if no alias can be built the identity is UNAVAILABLE.
rules.given: longName 'Advanced Micro Devices, Inc.'
rules.then: aliases = {'advanced micro devices inc', 'advanced micro devices'}, acronyms = {'amd'}, status RESOLVED
rules.parameters: Legal suffixes: inc, incorporated, corp, corporation, ltd, limited, llc, plc, co, company, sa, ag, nv, se, gmbh; ignored acronym words: the, and, of, for; alias min length 3; acronym length 3-6
edgeCases: Suffix stripping stops when one word remains
Two-letter acronyms dropped to avoid false positives
rules.suspectedDefect: Parity break: TS excludes an alias equal to the ticker (Yahoo shortName fallback) and uses companyName->longName->shortName for companyName, while Python accepts ticker-equal aliases and uses longName->shortName. A ticker-only shortName makes Python RESOLVED but TS UNAVAILABLE.

rules.name: Yahoo company identity derivation (aliases and acronyms)
rules.plainEnglish: Name aliases are built from Yahoo short and long names, normalized, with trailing legal suffixes stripped. Aliases need at least 3 characters. Acronyms are 3-6 initials, ignoring 'the/and/of/for'. Identity is RESOLVED only if at least one alias exists.
rules.given: longName 'Advanced Micro Devices, Inc.'
rules.then: aliases include 'advanced micro devices inc' and 'advanced micro devices', acronym 'amd', status RESOLVED
rules.parameters: Legal suffixes inc, incorporated, corp, corporation, ltd, limited, llc, plc, co, company, sa, ag, nv, se, gmbh; alias min length 3; acronym length 3-6
edgeCases: If identity lookup fails, status is UNAVAILABLE, only ticker-token matches are kept, and the SOURCE_IDENTITY_UNAVAILABLE warning makes collection PARTIAL

rules.name: Analyst valuation result status and method-not-disclosed list
rules.plainEnglish: Status is FOUND if any accepted evidence names a method, METHOD_NOT_DISCLOSED if there are targets without methods (from news or rating changes with a positive target), else NOT_FOUND; firms that published a target but never a method are listed once per source, and output is always CONTEXT_ONLY.
rules.given: News yields only 'Jefferies PT $50' and rating changes include Baird ptTo 45, ptFrom 0
rules.then: status = METHOD_NOT_DISCLOSED; methodNotDisclosed lists Jefferies (source news, target 50) and Baird (source rating_changes, target 45, prior null)
rules.and: Items are de-duplicated by URL (else title); evidence is capped at 40 rows; title truncated to 240 chars and sentence to 400 chars; decisionUse is always CONTEXT_ONLY.

edgeCases: The same firm can appear twice in methodNotDisclosed (once 'news', once 'rating_changes') because the keys are source-scoped
A firm with a method anywhere is excluded from methodNotDisclosed
Items with neither URL nor title are skipped

rules.name: Approved IR page status and allowed action: Python and Worker disagree

rules.then: Python: DISABLED / REVALIDATION_DUE / SOURCE_VALIDATION_FAILED all give allowedAction 'registry_review_required'. rules.smeQuestion: Which allowedAction values are canonical for DISABLED, REVALIDATION_DUE and SOURCE_VALIDATION_FAILED (planner decision on enum values)?

rules.name: Batch news per-ticker outcome state and partial-success metadata (Worker only)
rules.source: worker/src/yahoo-finance.ts:1246-1273; worker/src/yahoo-finance.ts:1297-1356; worker/src/yahoo-finance.ts:11959-11977; server.py:8328-8332; yfmcp/clients/yahoo.py:9-20; yfmcp/tools/pricing.py:21-44
rules.plainEnglish: In a multi-ticker news call, the Worker gives each ticker a success or error outcome. It classifies errors from the message text (contains 'not found' / 'no data found for ticker' / 'api error 404' -> TICKER_NOT_FOUND; contains 'timeout' -> PROVIDER_TIMEOUT, retryable; anything else -> PROVIDER_ERROR) and adds __batchMeta {partialSuccess, successCount, errorCount}. Python returns raw per-ticker payloads or {error, message, ticker}, with no codes and no batch metadata.
rules.given: get_company_news(['AAPL','ZZZZ']) where ZZZZ fails with the message 'No data found for ticker ZZZZ'
rules.then: Worker: AAPL -> its news payload; ZZZZ -> {error:true, code:'TICKER_NOT_FOUND', retryable:false, ...}; __batchMeta = {partialSuccess:true, successCount:1, errorCount:1}. Python: ZZZZ -> {error:true, message:..., ticker:'ZZZZ'} or the raw failure JSON, with no __batchMeta.
rules.parameters: BATCH_TICKER_CONCURRENCY = 3 (both runtimes); MAX_TICKERS = 5 (Worker rejects more; Python has no cap on this path); error codes TICKER_NOT_FOUND, PROVIDER_TIMEOUT (retryable), PROVIDER_ERROR
edgeCases: Worker trims whitespace from each ticker before fetching; Python does not trim, so ' AAPL ' is validated as-is
Worker treats any payload with a non-null 'error' key as a failure, even error:false
Worker error entries have different shapes by path: the shaped-error branch returns {error,code,message,retryable}, but the thrown-exception branch returns {ok:false,data:null,error:{...}}
partialSuccess is true only when there is at least one success and at least one error; all-fail gives partialSuccess=false
A duplicate ticker in the list overwrites its earlier entry in the keyed result in both runtimes
Tool description says 'only the first 5 are processed', but the Worker rejects lists longer than 5 with INPUT_VALIDATION_ERROR (worker/src/tools.ts:533 vs worker/src/yahoo-finance.ts:1301-1307)
rules.suspectedDefect: Python lacks __batchMeta and the error-code classification, a parity break. The Worker's error-entry shape depends on which failure path fired. Matching on the substring 'not found' can label unrelated failures as TICKER_NOT_FOUND.
rules.smeQuestion: Should Python emit the same per-ticker error codes and __batchMeta? Should the error-entry shape be standardised across both Worker failure paths?

rules.name: Collection status for news results
rules.plainEnglish: A news result is PARTIAL when it has items but some source was limited. An empty result is SOURCE_LIMITED_NOT_FOUND if a source was limited, NOT_FOUND if sources ran cleanly, and PROVIDER_ERROR if no source ran at all. A full result with clean sources has no status field.
rules.given: 0 items returned and a SOURCE_NOT_ELIGIBLE warning for Finnhub
rules.then: status = SOURCE_LIMITED_NOT_FOUND (not NOT_FOUND)
rules.parameters: limiting warning codes: SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, SOURCE_NOT_ELIGIBLE, SOURCE_IDENTITY_UNAVAILABLE, plus any COMPANY_IR_PAGE_* warning when the result is empty
edgeCases: Status is computed on the post-cap list. In search_company_news it is computed after query filtering
rules.suspectedDefect: Parity divergence. Python treats any COMPANY_IR_PAGE_* warning (including CANDIDATE_AVAILABLE and DISABLED) as limiting. The TS collectionStatus (worker/src/yahoo-finance.ts:10757-10776) lists only VALIDATION_FAILED, REVALIDATION_DUE and the company_ir RSS codes, so the two runtimes can return NOT_FOUND vs SOURCE_LIMITED_NOT_FOUND for the same case.

rules.name: Company IR RSS discovery lifecycle (rssDiscovery state)
rules.plainEnglish: Each company IR RSS lookup moves through discovery states: not_attempted, then website_not_available, feeds_discovered or feed_not_found, then feeds_accepted or feed_not_accepted. The source counts as used only if at least one feed was accepted.
rules.given: A ticker whose profile website yields 2 discovered feeds, both on external hosts that do not mention the company
rules.then: rssDiscovery = feed_not_accepted, two COMPANY_IR_RSS_HOST_REJECTED warnings are emitted, and used=false. A missing website gives rssDiscovery=website_not_available and used=false. Collection stops once maxResults items are gathered.
rules.parameters: acceptedFeeds reported: first 5
edgeCases: A feed that is accepted but whose items all fall outside the date window still gives used=true and EMPTY_RESULT

rules.name: Company IR page status and allowed action mapping
rules.plainEnglish: The company IR page source reports APPROVED_SOURCE_OK only when an approved page was fetched and returned items. Otherwise its status follows the registry warning, in this order: CANDIDATE_AVAILABLE, DISABLED, REVALIDATION_DUE, SOURCE_VALIDATION_FAILED, NOT_REGISTERED. Each status is paired with a next action.
rules.given: The ticker has a registry entry with status 'candidate'
rules.then: company_ir_page.status=CANDIDATE_AVAILABLE, allowedAction='review_and_promote', candidates=[the candidate record]
rules.parameters: allowedAction: APPROVED_SOURCE_OK->fetch_configured_source; CANDIDATE_AVAILABLE->review_and_promote; all others->registry_review_required
edgeCases: A fetch that runs but returns zero items gives EMPTY_RESULT with allowedAction registry_review_required

rules.name: Empty press-release result reports a 'no release' status even when a source failed
rules.plainEnglish: When no release items are found, the press-release status is chosen only from which sources were selected (Yahoo press releases, then company_ir_page, then company_ir, otherwise NOT_FOUND). Whether a source actually failed is not considered. The collection-status logic, which knows about source failures, runs only when there are items.
rules.given: get_company_press_releases with the default sources [sec, company_ir_page, yahoo_finance_press_releases], where SEC submissions are unavailable (SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE warning) and Yahoo returns no press releases
rules.then: status = NO_YAHOO_PRESS_RELEASE and coverageStatus = NO_OFFICIAL_RELEASE_SOURCE, not SOURCE_LIMITED_NOT_FOUND. The SEC failure appears only in sourceStatus and coverage.
rules.parameters: Status precedence: SEC_EX99_FOUND > APPROVED_IR_PAGE_FOUND > SEC_8K_FOUND_EX99_NOT_FOUND > (when empty) NO_YAHOO_PRESS_RELEASE | COMPANY_IR_PAGE_NOT_APPROVED / COMPANY_IR_PAGE_CANDIDATE_ONLY | COMPANY_IR_NOT_FOUND | NOT_FOUND > (when there are items) the collection status
edgeCases: When items exist, the status falls through to the collection status, which can return PARTIAL or null
If yahoo_finance_press_releases is selected, NO_YAHOO_PRESS_RELEASE wins even when the real gap is SEC or the IR page
rules.suspectedDefect: An empty result caused by a provider outage is labelled with a genuine-absence style status, which goes against the stated policy that source limits must be distinguishable from absence.
rules.smeQuestion: When a press-release call returns no items and at least one selected source failed (SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE), should status be SOURCE_LIMITED_NOT_FOUND instead of NO_YAHOO_PRESS_RELEASE / COMPANY_IR_NOT_FOUND / NOT_FOUND?

rules.name: Empty press-release status when only the IR-page registry is selected: Worker separates 'candidate only' from 'not approved'
rules.plainEnglish: If a press-release call returns nothing and company_ir_page is the deciding selected source, the Worker reports COMPANY_IR_PAGE_CANDIDATE_ONLY when the registry has unapproved candidates and COMPANY_IR_PAGE_NOT_APPROVED otherwise. Python always reports COMPANY_IR_PAGE_NOT_APPROVED.
rules.given: get_company_press_releases(ticker, sources=['company_ir_page']), with no approved IR page and one unapproved candidate registry entry for the ticker
rules.then: Worker: status = COMPANY_IR_PAGE_CANDIDATE_ONLY. Python: status = COMPANY_IR_PAGE_NOT_APPROVED. Both runtimes emit candidateSources, but from different inputs: Python reads COMPANY_IR_PAGE_CANDIDATE_AVAILABLE warnings, the Worker reads sourceDiagnostics.company_ir_page.candidates.
rules.parameters: Status values: COMPANY_IR_PAGE_CANDIDATE_ONLY (Worker only), COMPANY_IR_PAGE_NOT_APPROVED
edgeCases: If yahoo_finance_press_releases is also selected, NO_YAHOO_PRESS_RELEASE takes precedence in both runtimes
The two runtimes build candidateSources from different inputs, so the lists can differ even when both are present

rules.smeQuestion: Which status should both runtimes emit when only unapproved IR-page candidates exist: COMPANY_IR_PAGE_CANDIDATE_ONLY or COMPANY_IR_PAGE_NOT_APPROVED?

rules.name: Empty-result collection status treats IR page registry states differently per runtime
rules.plainEnglish: With zero items, Python reports SOURCE_LIMITED_NOT_FOUND for any COMPANY_IR_PAGE_* warning, including informational candidate or disabled entries. The Worker only does so for specific IR failure codes, and also for website/RSS discovery failures that Python never emits.
rules.given: sources=['sec','company_ir_page'], SEC returns nothing, and the ticker's IR page entry is 'candidate'
rules.then: Python: SOURCE_LIMITED_NOT_FOUND (the info warning COMPANY_IR_PAGE_CANDIDATE_AVAILABLE matches the prefix). Worker: no warning is emitted for candidates, so the status is NOT_FOUND.
rules.parameters: Worker list: COMPANY_WEBSITE_NOT_AVAILABLE, COMPANY_IR_FEED_NOT_FOUND, COMPANY_IR_RSS_HOST_REJECTED, COMPANY_IR_RSS_PARSE_ERROR, COMPANY_IR_RSS_UNAVAILABLE, COMPANY_IR_DISCOVERY_BUDGET_EXHAUSTED, COMPANY_IR_PAGE_VALIDATION_FAILED, COMPANY_IR_PAGE_REVALIDATION_DUE
edgeCases: Disabled entries: Python SOURCE_LIMITED_NOT_FOUND, Worker NOT_FOUND

rules.smeQuestion: Should an unreviewed candidate or disabled IR page make an empty result 'source-limited' (Python) or plain NOT_FOUND (Worker)?

rules.name: Expanded institutional ownership provider state machine
rules.plainEnglish: The tool tries Finnhub first, if the ticker is eligible. It moves to the scarce Alpha Vantage quota only when Finnhub gave no usable rows and the caller passed allow_scarce_fallback=true. A provider whose response names a different symbol is treated as a failure.
rules.given: Ticker AAPL. Finnhub returns OK, but payload.symbol is MSFT. allow_scarce_fallback=true
rules.then: The Finnhub attempt gets validationStatus PROVIDER_IDENTITY_MISMATCH, rows are discarded, and Alpha Vantage INSTITUTIONAL_HOLDINGS is called. If Alpha also yields no rows, status = Alpha's status, or NOT_FOUND when Alpha returned OK but empty.
rules.parameters: max_holders default 50, range 1-100; ownership cache TTL 7 days; capacityClass ENTITLEMENT_DEPENDENT (Finnhub) / SCARCE_SHARED_QUOTA (Alpha)
edgeCases: OK with zero rows becomes NOT_FOUND. Without fallback the action is VERIFY_SEC_13F_OR_ENABLE_SCARCE_FALLBACK.
A missing symbol in the response defaults to the requested ticker, so it passes.
Success: status OK, truncated = providerRowCount > returnedCount, freshnessStatus DATED or DATE_NOT_DISCLOSED, decisionGrade false, recommendedNextAction VERIFY_SEC_13F_FOR_MATERIAL_USE.

rules.name: Explicit source list selecting nothing forces SOURCE_LIMITED_NOT_FOUND
rules.plainEnglish: If the caller passes an explicit source list that contains no supported source (empty, or only unknown names), nothing is attempted. The result is marked source-limited, not a provider error or confirmed absence.
rules.given: get_company_news('AAPL', sources=['bloomberg'])
rules.then: status = SOURCE_LIMITED_NOT_FOUND, sourceCoverage = PARTIAL, coverage.state = PARTIAL, recommendedNextAction = CHECK_OFFICIAL_RELEASES, plus a SOURCE_UNSUPPORTED warning
rules.parameters: none
edgeCases: This overrides the PROVIDER_ERROR that the collection-status logic would otherwise give for no sources used
Omitting sources (null) never triggers it

rules.name: Explicit source list with no supported source reads as source-limited
rules.plainEnglish: If the caller passes an explicit source list in which no source is supported, nothing is attempted. The result is SOURCE_LIMITED_NOT_FOUND with PARTIAL coverage and a recommendation to check official releases, never a plain NOT_FOUND.
rules.given: sources=['bloomberg']
rules.when: search_company_news, get_company_press_releases, get_public_event_timeline or verify_company_event finishes
rules.then: status='SOURCE_LIMITED_NOT_FOUND', sourceCoverage='PARTIAL', coverage.state='PARTIAL', coverage.recommendedNextAction='CHECK_OFFICIAL_RELEASES'
edgeCases: sources=None (defaults) is never overridden
The final status is overwritten even if earlier logic set a different status

rules.name: Finnhub status state machine (eligibility, configuration, HTTP outcome, truncation)
rules.plainEnglish: Finnhub's status is chosen in a fixed order: NOT_ELIGIBLE, then OK/EMPTY_RESULT if it was used, then UNCONFIGURED, AUTH_ERROR, RATE_LIMITED, PROVIDER_CHANGED, PROVIDER_ERROR, and finally EMPTY_RESULT. The state is read by matching text in warning messages.
rules.given: Finnhub returned 30 in-window items and the cap returned 10
rules.then: finnhub.status = OK, acceptedCount 30, returnedCount 10, truncatedCount 20, hasMoreAccepted = true
rules.parameters: Message substrings checked: 'finnhub company-news source is not configured', 'finnhub auth error', 'finnhub rate limited', 'finnhub provider changed', 'finnhub'
edgeCases: A Finnhub timeout is never classified as TIMEOUT. It becomes PROVIDER_ERROR because the collector only special-cases HTTP 401/403/429 (server.py:1744-1770)
An UNCONFIGURED status has no rawCount or filteredCount fields
rules.suspectedDefect: Status is derived from free-text warning messages, so rewording a message silently changes the state. Finnhub cannot report TIMEOUT, which means RETRY_RETRYABLE_SOURCES never fires for a Finnhub timeout.

rules.name: Marketaux status mapping from HTTP and parse outcome
rules.plainEnglish: Marketaux moves from an initial PROVIDER_ERROR to a final state: UNCONFIGURED (no token), AUTH_ERROR (401/403), RATE_LIMITED (402/429), TIMEOUT, PROVIDER_ERROR, PROVIDER_CHANGED (no data array), or OK/EMPTY_RESULT. Each state has an allowed next action.
rules.given: Marketaux returns HTTP 402
rules.then: status = RATE_LIMITED, allowedAction = retry_after_quota_reset, and coverage.recommendedNextAction = RETRY_RETRYABLE_SOURCES
rules.parameters: allowedAction map: NOT_NEEDED->none, UNCONFIGURED->configure_marketaux_api_token, AUTH_ERROR->verify_marketaux_api_token, RATE_LIMITED->retry_after_quota_reset, TIMEOUT->retry_later, PROVIDER_CHANGED->inspect_provider_contract, PROVIDER_ERROR->retry_or_use_official_sources, OK with items->check_official_releases
edgeCases: TIMEOUT is detected by 'timeout' or 'timed out' in the exception text
An unknown status with 0 accepted items maps to allowedAction 'none'

rules.name: One Yahoo outage warning marks every selected Yahoo sub-source as PROVIDER_ERROR
rules.plainEnglish: If a selected Yahoo source has no per-source diagnostic and was not used, its status is PROVIDER_ERROR whenever any SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE warning mentions 'yahoo finance', and EMPTY_RESULT otherwise. A single outage message therefore fails news, press releases and the legacy aggregate together. When a diagnostic exists, it wins: completed=false gives PROVIDER_ERROR, otherwise acceptedCount > 0 gives OK, else EMPTY_RESULT.
rules.given: sources = [yahoo_finance_news, yahoo_finance_press_releases], no collector diagnostics, and one warning {code: SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, message: 'Yahoo Finance news unavailable'}
rules.then: Both yahoo_finance_news and yahoo_finance_press_releases = {status: PROVIDER_ERROR, rawCount: 0, filteredCount: 0}
rules.parameters: Match = case-insensitive substring 'yahoo finance' in SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE messages; precedence = diagnostic > used-in-sourcesUsed > outage text > EMPTY_RESULT. In Python, when selected_sources is None the selection defaults to [yahoo_finance_news, yahoo_finance_press_releases, finnhub, marketaux]; the Worker requires an explicit selection
edgeCases: The legacy yahoo_finance aggregate counts items tagged with any of the three Yahoo source names
Python coerces counts with int(x or 0) while the Worker uses Number(x ?? 0); a non-numeric count gives 0 in Python and NaN in the Worker
An IDENTITY_UNAVAILABLE identity diagnostic is shown as a separate yahoo_finance_identity entry
rules.smeQuestion: Should a Yahoo outage be attributed to each sub-source separately, or is failing all Yahoo sub-sources together on one outage message intended?

rules.name: Overall collection status
rules.plainEnglish: A news response is PARTIAL when items exist but a source was unavailable/ineligible/identity-limited; when empty it is SOURCE_LIMITED_NOT_FOUND if any source was limited (or an IR page problem), NOT_FOUND if sources ran cleanly, else PROVIDER_ERROR.
rules.given: No items returned and Finnhub unconfigured
rules.then: status = SOURCE_LIMITED_NOT_FOUND (empty may reflect missing coverage, not absence)
rules.parameters: Limiting warning codes: SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, SOURCE_NOT_ELIGIBLE, SOURCE_IDENTITY_UNAVAILABLE, COMPANY_IR_PAGE_*
edgeCases: Items present with no limits -> no status field

rules.name: Per-source news status: Yahoo feed state from collector completion and accepted count
rules.plainEnglish: Each Yahoo news feed gets one of three states: PROVIDER_ERROR if the fetch did not finish, OK if at least one item was accepted, otherwise EMPTY_RESULT.
rules.given: get_company_news runs with source yahoo_finance_news, and the Yahoo collector finished (completed=true) with rawCount 20, rejected 20, acceptedCount 0
rules.then: yahoo_finance_news.status = EMPTY_RESULT, rawCount 20, rejectedCount 20, rejectionCounts broken down by reason (e.g. IDENTITY_MISMATCH, DATE_WINDOW). If completed=false the status is PROVIDER_ERROR whatever the counts are.

edgeCases: The legacy 'yahoo_finance' aggregate is completed only if every sub-feed completed (server.py:2700)
When there are no diagnostics, the code falls back to 'Yahoo Finance' text in SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE warning messages (server.py:2203-2206)

rules.name: Per-source status for SEC, company_ir and newswire
rules.plainEnglish: Each source's status is OK if it ran and returned items, and EMPTY_RESULT if it ran with none. If it did not run, the status is PROVIDER_ERROR when a SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE warning names that provider, otherwise EMPTY_RESULT.
rules.given: The SEC was selected but not used, and a warning reads 'SEC submissions fetch failed'
rules.then: sec.status=PROVIDER_ERROR with rawCount 0. With no such warning, sec.status=EMPTY_RESULT
rules.parameters: Warning substrings: 'sec submissions' (SEC), 'yahoo finance' (company_ir), 'globenewswire' (newswire)
edgeCases: company_ir errors are keyed off 'yahoo finance' warnings, not IR-specific ones
rawCount equals filteredCount for these sources
rules.smeQuestion: Is it intended that a company_ir source failure is detected only from a 'yahoo finance' warning, and that an unattempted source with no warning reports EMPTY_RESULT instead of an error?

rules.name: SEC source status: no CIK or submissions means provider error, not absence
rules.plainEnglish: When SEC is a selected news source, its status is OK if SEC items came back, EMPTY_RESULT if SEC was read but nothing matched, and PROVIDER_ERROR if the ticker could not be resolved to an SEC CIK or its submissions could not be loaded.

rules.when: The SEC collector cannot load submissions and emits SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE 'SEC submissions source unavailable.'
rules.then: sourceStatus.sec = {status: PROVIDER_ERROR, rawCount 0}; sourceCoverage becomes PARTIAL; with zero items overall the collection status is SOURCE_LIMITED_NOT_FOUND rather than NOT_FOUND
rules.parameters: Status derived by substring match 'sec submissions' on SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE warning messages

rejectedRules.plainEnglish: Search collects up to 100 items over 14 days, keeps those whose title/summary/source/eventType/evidence text contains the query (case-insensitive substring), ranks by relevance and caps at max results.
rejectedRules.then: Python returns INPUT_VALIDATION_ERROR 'query is required'; TS returns all collected items unfiltered
edgeCases: Query 'earnings' also matches eventType label
rejectedRules.suspectedDefect: Parity break on empty/whitespace query (Python rejects, TS returns everything); TS also reports matchCount which Python's visible code path was not confirmed to emit.
rejectedRules.smeQuestion: Should an empty query be rejected in both runtimes?
rejectedRules.rejectionReason:
refuted: The filter itself is real and matches in both runtimes. The rule is wrong about empty queries and points at the wrong TS function.

What holds: server.py:2735-2775 collects with max_results=100 and lookback_days=14. It lowercases the query and keeps an item only if the query appears in its title, summary, source, eventType or evidenceText. It then ranks by relevance and caps at _coerce_max_results(max_results, 10). An empty or whitespace query returns INPUT_VALIDATION_ERROR 'query is required' (server.py:2746-2747).

Wrong TS citation: worker/src/yahoo-finance.ts:11964-11985 is the end of getCompanyNews, not search. The real function is searchCompanyNews at worker/src/yahoo-finance.ts:11987-12028. It uses the same 100/14 pool and the same five-field case-insensitive substring filter, then ranks and slices with clampInt(maxResults, 10, 1, 100).

Why refuted: the Then clause says TS returns every collected item unfiltered when the query is empty. That is wrong at the tool level. The Worker's dispatcher at worker/src/tools.ts:2519-2522 returns mcpFailure(INPUT_VALIDATION_ERROR, 'query is required') for an empty query before searchCompanyNews is ever called. The unfiltered fallback (the ternary at yahoo-finance.ts:12006-12008, `q ? filter : out.items`) only runs if something calls searchCompanyNews directly. Through MCP, both runtimes reject an empty query the same way, so the claimed Python/TS split does not exist.

No instruction-shaped text in the cited regions.

rejectedRules.name: Event verification status lifecycle (CONFIRMED / PARTIAL / STALE / NOT_FOUND / SOURCE_LIMITED_NOT_FOUND / CONFLICTING)
rejectedRules.plainEnglish: An event is CONFIRMED when a matching official-source item with a URL and HIGH/MEDIUM confidence falls in range. It is PARTIAL when only non-official matches are in range, STALE when every match is older than 90 days, and NOT_FOUND otherwise. NOT_FOUND becomes SOURCE_LIMITED_NOT_FOUND when coverage failed, and that state is retryable for subrequest limit, rate limit or timeout.
rejectedRules.given: event_query 'BlueBird satellite launch' (3 meaningful terms, so 2 must match) and only a Yahoo news match dated within 90 days
rejectedRules.then: status PARTIAL. If the only match were 120 days old: STALE. With no match and Finnhub RATE_LIMITED: SOURCE_LIMITED_NOT_FOUND with failureMode RATE_LIMITED and retryable true
rejectedRules.parameters: _STALE_EVENT_DAYS=90; lookback 365; term threshold ceil(0.67 x terms) when there are more than 2 terms; min term length 3; stopwords (announce, news, press, release, results ...)
rejectedRules.smeQuestion: CONFLICTING depends on EVIDENCE_CONFLICT warnings, which nothing in server.py emits. The LOW_RELEVANCE downgrade (CONFIRMED to PARTIAL) cannot fire because every collector sets tickers=[ticker], which scores HIGH. Are these states meant to be live?
rejectedRules.suspectedDefect: (1) CONFLICTING is unreachable: EVIDENCE_CONFLICT is only read (server.py:3264, worker/src/yahoo-finance.ts:12367), never produced. (2) server.py:3381 passes the raw `sources` argument (None by default) to _compute_source_status, which then defaults to the four news sources. With default sources, the sec, company_ir_page and company_ir statuses are omitted from sourceStatus and coverage even though they were collected, so their failures cannot trigger SOURCE_LIMITED_NOT_FOUND.
edgeCases: A failure mode of WORKER_SUBREQUEST_LIMIT is detected from 'too many subrequests' in warning text
Failure-mode precedence: subrequest limit > RATE_LIMITED > TIMEOUT > PROVIDER_CHANGED > IDENTITY_UNAVAILABLE > UNCONFIGURED > NOT_ELIGIBLE > PROVIDER_ERROR
rejectedRules.rejectionReason:
refuted: The citation points to the right code, and most of the rule is accurate. The STALE condition is wrong, though, and the rule's own STALE example gives a different result when you trace the code.

What the code does match:
- The constant is `_STALE_EVENT_DAYS = 90` (server.py:229).
- The lookback is 365 days (server.py:3190).
- The stopword set is at server.py:3196-3201.
- Meaningful terms must be at least 3 characters and not stopwords (server.py:3203-3206).
- The number of terms that must match is all of them when there are 2 or fewer, otherwise ceil(0.67 x terms) (server.py:3207-3211). Three terms therefore need 2 matches.
- An item counts as official only if its sourceType is official, it has a URL and its confidence is HIGH or MEDIUM (server.py:3243-3248). Yahoo news is not an official source type (server.py:237).
- The order of checks is CONFLICTING, then CONFIRMED, PARTIAL, STALE, NOT_FOUND (server.py:3268-3277).
- If coverage failed, NOT_FOUND becomes SOURCE_LIMITED_NOT_FOUND (server.py:3385-3392).
- `retryable` is true only for WORKER_SUBREQUEST_LIMIT, RATE_LIMITED or PROVIDER_TIMEOUT (server.py:3393-3394).

Where the rule is wrong:
- At server.py:3238-3242, `matched_in_range` includes every match whenever no start_date and no end_date are given, because of the clause `or (not start_date and not end_date)`.
- STALE is only checked after PARTIAL (server.py:3274), so STALE needs `matched_in_range` to be empty. That can only happen when the caller gives a date window and every match falls outside it.
- So in the rule's example, with no dates and one 120-day-old match, the status is PARTIAL, not STALE. "STALE when every match is older than 90 days" is not what the code does.

Smaller things the rule leaves out:
- CONFLICTING (server.py:3256-3269) is checked first and overrides everything else. The rule never says when it applies.
- When every evidence item has LOW relevance, CONFIRMED is downgraded to PARTIAL (server.py:3371-3379). This is the second cited range, but the rule does not mention it.

The PARTIAL and SOURCE_LIMITED_NOT_FOUND/RATE_LIMITED parts of the example would hold, assuming `_verify_coverage_failure_mode` returns RATE_LIMITED; I did not open that helper. I found no instruction-shaped text in the cited lines.

rejectedRules.name: SEC recent events: empty filing_types handled differently
rejectedRules.plainEnglish: Python rejects an empty filing-type list. The Worker treats it as 'all forms'.
rejectedRules.then: Python returns INPUT_VALIDATION_ERROR 'filing_types must not be empty'. Worker returns up to max_results filings of any form type (Form 4, S-8, etc.) within 90 days.
rejectedRules.parameters: default filing types 8-K, 10-Q, 10-K; lookback clamp 1-3650; max clamp 1-100
edgeCases: The Worker sets sec status to PROVIDER_ERROR when SEC submissions are unavailable, otherwise OK/EMPTY_RESULT
rejectedRules.suspectedDefect: Parity break: the Worker silently widens the request instead of rejecting it.
rejectedRules.rejectionReason:
refuted: The Worker half of the rule is right. The Python half is wrong, so the rule as written is refuted.

Worker: worker/src/tools.ts:2541 passes an empty array through unchanged. It only falls back to the 8-K/10-Q/10-K default when the argument is not an array. In worker/src/yahoo-finance.ts:11101-11105 the filter is `wanted.size > 0 && !wanted.has(form)`. An empty set therefore lets every form through. Results are capped by clampInt(maxResults,20,1,100) and the lookback by clampInt(lookbackDays,90,1,3650) (yahoo-finance.ts:12246). So filing_types=[] gives filings of any type.

Python: server.py:3094 builds the list with `(filing_types or ["8-K", "10-Q", "10-K"])`. An empty list is falsy in Python, so [] is replaced by the three default types and the call succeeds. It does not return INPUT_VALIDATION_ERROR. The 'filing_types must not be empty' error at server.py:3095-3096 only fires when the list has entries but all of them are blank, e.g. [""] or ["  "]. Those are dropped by the `if str(ft).strip()` filter.

The two runtimes do diverge, but not as described. With [], Python returns the defaults (8-K/10-Q/10-K) and the Worker returns all forms. With blank-only entries, Python returns the error, and the Worker builds a set containing "" or "  ". No real form matches that, so it most likely returns an empty result (inferred; not traced further). The parameter clamps listed in the rule are accurate. The cited lines contain no instruction-shaped text.

rejectedRules.name: DCF assumption extraction (WACC, discount rate, terminal growth, exit multiple)
rejectedRules.plainEnglish: When a sentence mentions a DCF or discounted cash flow, the WACC, discount rate, terminal growth rate and exit multiple are picked up if they are quoted.
rejectedRules.given: The sentence 'Our DCF assumes a 9.5% WACC and 3% terminal growth, with a 12x exit multiple'
rejectedRules.and: Each rate first tries 'LABEL ... N%' (up to 20 non-digit, non-% characters between label and number), then 'N% LABEL'. Each value is taken from the first match only.
rejectedRules.parameters: Percent values 1-2 integer digits (0-99.x); exit multiple 1-3 digits followed by 'x'; label gap 20 chars
edgeCases: A rate of 100% or more cannot be captured
A DCF method is recorded even when no parameters are found (all null)
rejectedRules.rejectionReason:
refuted: The cited lines are the right place, and the overall shape matches. If the sentence mentions DCF or discounted cash flow, the code builds a DCF entry. Each rate tries the label-first regex `LABEL[^%\d]{0,20}(\d{1,2}(?:\.\d+)?)\s?%` and falls back to `N% LABEL`. Python and TS behave the same (yfmcp/capital_structure.py:3161-3163, 3190-3197; worker/src/capital-structure.ts:2883-2886, 2903-2911). But the rule's worked example and part of its spec do not match what the code does.

I ran the actual regexes on the example sentence 'Our DCF assumes a 9.5% WACC and 3% terminal growth, with a 12x exit multiple':
(1) waccPct comes out as 3, not 9.5. The label-first pattern matches 'WACC and 3%': the gap ' and ' has no digit or %, so it grabs the terminal-growth figure. The fallback '9.5% WACC' is never tried.
(2) terminalGrowthPct = 3 is correct, but it comes from the fallback '3% terminal growth' pattern.
(3) exitMultiple comes out as null, not 12. Only a label-first pattern exists for it, `(?:terminal|exit) multiple[^\d]{0,20}(\d{1,3}...)\s?x`, and there is no 'Nx exit multiple' fallback. So the spec's 'then N% LABEL' claim does not apply to exit multiple.
(4) discountRatePct = null is correct.

The rule also leaves out details. The terminal label is 'terminal (growth )?(rate )?', so plain 'terminal' works too. Exit multiple accepts 'terminal multiple' as well as 'exit multiple'. Its gap only excludes digits, not %.

Because the stated Given/When/Then output (WACC 9.5, exit multiple 12) is not what the code produces, the rule as written is refuted. The code's real behaviour picks up the wrong WACC here, which looks like a genuine extraction bug worth flagging. I found no instruction-shaped text in the cited region.

rejectedRules.name: Analyst valuation method detection from news sentences
rejectedRules.plainEnglish: Each news sentence is scanned for named valuation methods: an 'N x metric' or 'metric of N x' multiple (with EV flag and forecast periods), DCF (with WACC, discount rate, terminal growth and exit multiple when stated), sum-of-the-parts, risk-adjusted NPV, probability-weighted scenarios and peer comparison.
rejectedRules.given: A news sentence 'Needham values the stock at 41x 2H27 EV/EBITDA using a DCF with a 9.5% WACC and 3% terminal growth'
rejectedRules.then: Two methods are recorded: {method:multiple, multiple:41, metric:EBITDA, enterpriseValue:true, periods:['2H27']} and {method:DCF, waccPct:9.5, terminalGrowthPct:3, discountRatePct:null, exitMultiple:null}
rejectedRules.and: A multiple whose window contains than/grew/growth/increase(d/s)/faster/more is rejected as not a multiple (e.g. '3x faster revenue growth'); duplicate multiple|metric|EV combinations in a sentence are counted once; multiples must be > 0 and 1-3 integer digits.
rejectedRules.parameters: Multiple: 1-3 digits (+decimals) followed by x/times within 40 chars of metric (metric-first form: 30 chars after); percentages 1-2 digits; exit multiple 1-3 digits + 'x'; period tokens FYxx, CYxx, Fxx, 1H/2Hxx, 19xx/20xx(E), NTM, next twelve months, forward
edgeCases: P/E, EPS and 'earnings' normalize to metric 'earnings'; price-to-sales, revenue and sales to 'sales'; EV/revenue becomes 'sales' with enterpriseValue true
'next twelve months' is normalized to NTM
EV flag is set when the window mentions EV or 'enterprise value' even if the metric is not EV/x
rejectedRules.rejectionReason:
refuted: The citation points to the right code, and most of the rule matches it. Both runtimes have the same per-sentence detector: worker/src/capital-structure.ts:2888-2917 (sentenceMethods) and yfmcp/capital_structure.py:3170-3206 (_sentence_methods). The shared patterns are at TS 2833-2837 and PY 3093-3097. What matches: the multiple-first form allows 1-3 digits plus x/times within 40 chars of the metric, and the metric-first form allows 30 chars after. A window containing than/grew/growth/increase[sd]/faster/more is rejected (TS 2892, PY 3175). Repeat multiple|metric|EV keys are dropped, and the multiple must be > 0 (TS 2895-2896, PY 3179-3180). The EV flag and periods come from the window. The period tokens match the rule's list, and the 1-2 digit percentages and 3-digit 'x' exit multiple also match. The SOTP, rNPV, probability-weighted and peer-comparison checks are there too.

The worked example does not hold, though. In the sentence '...a DCF with a 9.5% WACC and 3% terminal growth', the code tries the WACC-first pattern before anything else: /\bWACC\b[^%\d]{0,20}(\d{1,2}(?:\.\d+)?)\s?%/ (TS 2906, PY 3193). That pattern skips ' and ' after 'WACC' and captures '3'. The '9.5% WACC' pattern is only a fallback for when the first one finds nothing, so it never runs here. I ran the Python pattern on the example sentence and it returned 3. So the DCF record comes out as waccPct:3, not waccPct:9.5 as the rule states. terminalGrowthPct:3 is correct, via the fallback pattern. The multiple record {41, EBITDA, enterpriseValue:true, periods:['2H27']} is also correct.

Because the rule's own Given/When/Then example gives the wrong output, it does not describe the behaviour accurately. If it is rewritten, it should state the real precedence: a percentage after 'WACC' within 20 non-digit characters wins over one before it. That also means a WACC given as 'N% WACC' can be assigned a later, unrelated percentage. I found no instruction-like text in the cited lines.

rejectedRules.name: Analyst valuation-method extraction status (FOUND / METHOD_NOT_DISCLOSED / NOT_FOUND)
rejectedRules.plainEnglish: News items and rating changes are scanned for named valuation methods and price targets. The result is FOUND if any accepted evidence names a method, METHOD_NOT_DISCLOSED if there are only targets or rating-change targets, and NOT_FOUND otherwise. It is always context-only.
rejectedRules.given: One news item 'Cantor reiterates $122 target on Rocket Lab' with no method, and one rating change Jefferies ptTo 50
rejectedRules.when: extract_analyst_valuation_methods runs with issuer name 'Rocket Lab USA, Inc.'
rejectedRules.then: status METHOD_NOT_DISCLOSED. methodNotDisclosed lists Cantor (source news) and Jefferies (source rating_changes, prior null if ptFrom<=0). decisionUse CONTEXT_ONLY, basis NEWS_TEXT_EXTRACTION.
rejectedRules.parameters: evidence capped at 40; title truncated to 240 chars, sentence to 400; items de-duplicated by URL, else by title; firm list = rating-change firms first, then built-in BROKERS
edgeCases: A sentence counts only if it has a method, or both a target and a recognised firm.
A firm that disclosed a method anywhere is left out of methodNotDisclosed.
A rating change with ptTo <= 0 or non-numeric is ignored.
rejectedRules.rejectionReason:
refuted: Most of the rule is right, but the worked example would fail if you ran it. The headline status, decisionUse and basis come out as the rule says. The methodNotDisclosed list does not: Cantor never gets onto it.

What the code does, the same in both runtimes (yfmcp/capital_structure.py:3294-3406 and worker/src/capital-structure.ts:2992-3085):
- **Status:** FOUND if any accepted evidence names a method. METHOD_NOT_DISCLOSED if there is any evidence or any methodNotDisclosed entry. NOT_FOUND otherwise (py:3384-3389, ts:3069). basis is NEWS_TEXT_EXTRACTION and decisionUse is CONTEXT_ONLY (py:3393-3394).
- **Firm list:** firms from the rating changes come first, then the built-in BROKERS list minus case-insensitive duplicates (py:3304-3305).
- **De-duplication:** items are keyed by URL, or by title when there is no URL (py:3312-3316).
- **Truncation:** title to 240 characters, sentence to 400 (py:3348-3349).
- **Evidence cap:** only the returned evidence list is cut to 40 (py:3398). Every item still counts towards the status and the method counts.
- **Rating changes:** a change is listed when ptTo > 0, with source rating_changes, prior set to null when ptFrom <= 0, and url null (py:3365-3378).
- **Function name:** the function is analyst_valuation_methods (analystValuationMethods in TS), not extract_analyst_valuation_methods.

Why the example fails:
1. Firm names are matched case-sensitively as whole words in _firm_in (py:3234-3243).
2. BROKERS has "Cantor Fitzgerald" but no plain "Cantor" (py:3074-3083). The headline 'Cantor reiterates $122 target on Rocket Lab' only says "Cantor", so no firm is found.
3. That sentence names no method and its target has no firm, so it is skipped and never becomes evidence (py:3329-3330, ts:3018).
4. With no evidence, there is no news entry for Cantor in methodNotDisclosed (py:3357-3364).

The status is still METHOD_NOT_DISCLOSED, but only because of the Jefferies rating change (ptTo 50). methodNotDisclosed contains only Jefferies (source rating_changes), not Cantor (source news) as the example claims.

To fix the example, write the headline as "Cantor Fitzgerald reiterates...", or move Cantor into the rating changes. No instruction-shaped text was found in the cited code.

rejectedRules.name: Price-target subject attribution (CLAUSE / ITEM / rejected)
rejectedRules.plainEnglish: When the issuer name is known, a target or method is kept only if its own clause names the company (CLAUSE), or the sentence names no company while the item names the subject and no sentence gives another company's target (ITEM). Anything else is counted in rejectedForOtherCompany.
rejectedRules.given: Ticker RKLB, names ['Rocket Lab USA, Inc.'], headline 'AST SpaceMobile rises; Cantor reiterates $122 target on Rocket Lab'
rejectedRules.then: The clause '... $122 target on Rocket Lab' names the alias 'rocket lab usa', so subjectMatch=CLAUSE. Aliases are the ticker base if 3+ chars and the normalized name with and without trailing legal suffixes (inc, corp, plc, holdings, group...).
rejectedRules.parameters: alias min length 3; clauses split on '; ' and ', '; LEGAL_SUFFIXES set of 17 words
edgeCases: Without issuer names, subjectMatch=NOT_CHECKED and nothing is rejected.
Tickers of 1-2 letters (e.g. 'F') contribute no ticker alias.
Alias match needs the whole phrase after normalization, so 'Rocket Lab' alone does not match the alias 'rocket lab usa' unless the name yields it.
rejectedRules.rejectionReason:
refuted: The general mechanism is real, but the rule's worked example claims an outcome the code would not produce, so the rule as written does not hold.

What matches, in both runtimes:
- The suffix set has 17 words (yfmcp/capital_structure.py:3258, worker/src/capital-structure.ts:2955).
- Aliases are built in subject_aliases / subjectAliases (py:3265-3281, ts:2962-2974): the ticker base if it is 3+ characters, plus the normalized name with and without its trailing suffixes, each kept only if 3+ characters.
- The subject match is whole-phrase matching on normalized text (py:3284-3286, ts:2976-2979).
- Clauses split on ";" and ", " (py:3291, ts:2983).
- The 'conflicted' check matches the description (py:3322-3324, ts:3012-3013).
- The three-way decision is as described: CLAUSE if the clause names the subject; ITEM if the sentence names no alias, the item does, and the item is not conflicted; otherwise rejected_other_company is incremented and the sentence is skipped (py:3332-3340, ts:3020-3028).
- No attribution check runs when issuer names are absent (py:3302, ts:2993).

What does not match: the Given/Then example. For ticker RKLB and name 'Rocket Lab USA, Inc.', the code builds the aliases {'rklb', 'rocket lab usa inc', 'rocket lab usa'}. Only 'inc' is stripped, because 'usa' is not in the suffix set. The headline's target clause 'Cantor reiterates $122 target on Rocket Lab' normalizes to '... target on rocket lab'. That contains none of the aliases: 'rocket lab usa' is not a substring of it. So the clause check fails. The sentence also names no alias, and the headline-only item does not name the subject either. The code would therefore count this headline in rejectedForOtherCompany, not return subjectMatch=CLAUSE. I worked this through by reading the code; I did not run it.

The cited lines contain no instruction-shaped text.

rejectedRules.name: SEC recent events: invalid SEC Archives URL downgrades confidence (Python only)
rejectedRules.plainEnglish: In Python's get_sec_recent_events, any item without an https://www.sec.gov/Archives/ URL is set to LOW confidence and gets an SEC_URL_INVALID warning. The Worker does neither. Python also computes sourceStatus but does not return it, while the Worker returns sourceStatus, sourceCoverage and coverage.
rejectedRules.given: An 8-K submission row with no accession number, so no Archives URL can be built
rejectedRules.then: Python: confidence=LOW and warning SEC_URL_INVALID, with no sourceStatus or coverage fields in the payload. Worker: confidence comes from buildSecEventItem (LOW here anyway), with no SEC_URL_INVALID warning, and sourceStatus.sec plus sourceCoverage and coverage are included.
rejectedRules.parameters: Allowed URL prefix https://www.sec.gov/Archives/; warning code SEC_URL_INVALID
edgeCases: Python's source_status and source_coverage variables (server.py:3115-3116) are computed and then discarded
rejectedRules.suspectedDefect: The output shape differs between runtimes (missing coverage fields and a warning code that exists only in Python).
rejectedRules.rejectionReason: refuted: The Python half is accurate. In server.py:3105-3112, any item that fails _safe_sec_url (server.py:935-937, which requires the prefix https://www.sec.gov/Archives/) is set to confidence LOW and gets an SEC_URL_INVALID warning. sourceStatus and source_coverage are computed at server.py:3115-3116 but never added to the payload (server.py:3117-3128). The Worker cite is also right that getSecRecentEvents (worker/src/yahoo-finance.ts:12240-12262) returns sourceStatus, sourceCoverage and coverage, and does no URL check of its own. The core claim is wrong, though: the rule says this is Python-only, that the Worker does neither, and that the Worker gives no SEC_URL_INVALID warning. getSecRecentEvents calls collectSecEvents, which calls buildSecEventItem (worker/src/yahoo-finance.ts:11114). There, at worker/src/yahoo-finance.ts:10690-10692, any URL that does not start with https://www.sec.gov/Archives/ is blanked and gets the same SEC_URL_INVALID warning, and confidence comes out LOW when the URL is empty (worker/src/yahoo-finance.ts:10698). Those warnings are added to sec.warnings (worker/src/yahoo-finance.ts:11118), which the payload returns at worker/src/yahoo-finance.ts:12256. For the stated case (no accession number), the Worker also emits SEC_URL_INVALID with confidence LOW. The URL check is not a Python-only divergence; it is only placed differently in the two runtimes. The real difference is only the missing sourceStatus/coverage fields in Python's payload. No instruction-shaped text was found in the cited lines.

rejectedRules.name: News event-type keyword lists differ between runtimes
rejectedRules.plainEnglish: Both runtimes classify a headline into the first matching category, but Python's keyword lists contain extra terms the Worker lacks: 'annual report' (earnings), 'credit facility' (financing), 'announces new' (product), and 10-Q/10-K under regulatory.
rejectedRules.given: A headline 'Acme announces new widget line' with no other keywords
rejectedRules.then: Python returns 'product' via 'announces new'. The Worker also returns 'product', but only through 'product'. For 'Acme enters $500M credit facility' Python returns 'financing', while the Worker returns 'other' (no 'offering|financing|debt|note' match). For 'Acme files annual report' Python returns 'earnings' and the Worker returns 'regulatory' (via 'filing').
rejectedRules.parameters: Order: earnings, guidance, contract, financing, product, analyst, macro, litigation, insider, regulatory, other
edgeCases: Both runtimes match substrings without word boundaries, so 'eps' matches 'steps' and 'sec' matches 'second' or 'sector'
'note' in Python and 'notes?' in the Worker match 'denote' and 'footnote'
rejectedRules.suspectedDefect: eventType and the decisionUse derived from it (server.py:427-430) can differ between runtimes for the same headline.
rejectedRules.rejectionReason:
refuted: The citation is correct, and the main claim holds. Python `_event_type_from_keywords` (server.py:633-655) and Worker `eventTypeFromKeywords` (worker/src/yahoo-finance.ts:9622-9635) both return the first matching category, in the same order. Python has keywords the Worker lacks: 'annual report' (635), 'credit facility' (641), 'announces new' (643), and '10-q'/'10-k' under regulatory (653). Those last two can never fire, because the earnings check (Python 635, Worker 9624) catches them first. The 'credit facility' example is also right: Python returns 'financing' and the Worker returns 'other'.

The Specification still fails on two of its three examples when traced against the code:
1. 'Acme announces new widget line': the headline does not contain the word 'product', and nothing else in /launch|product|introduce/ (9628) matches. No later Worker pattern matches either (sec, rates, notes?, and so on), so the Worker returns 'other', not 'product'. These are real parity differences, not matching results.
2. 'Acme files annual report': the Worker's regulatory regex /sec|regulatory|8-k|filing/ (9633) does not match 'files', because 'files' does not contain 'filing', and no other pattern matches. The Worker returns 'other', not 'regulatory'.

Two smaller points the rule leaves out. The Worker classifies the title and summary joined together (9623), while Python takes one text argument. The Worker's /notes?/ is the same in effect as Python's 'note'. Because the stated Given/When/Then results are wrong for a P1 calculation rule, the rule as written is refuted, even though the keyword-list difference it describes is real. No instruction-shaped text was found in the cited lines.
